method: Introduces 'hidden dependence' for random vectors and proves that small probability-distance perturbations of a reference joint law (marginals fixed) attain the same unconstrained worst-case bounds for gamma-tail risk measures; illustrates with a stylised credit-loan portfolio.
reason: All numerics are analytic illustrations on assumed homogeneous credit portfolios (n=500 or 50,000, p=0.01, rho=0.10) with a Gaussian reference copula. No dataset of any kind is used, so there is nothing measured on real market data to replicate.

method: Characterises the full set of increasing profits (a strong arbitrage) in a one-dimensional general-diffusion market with a constant-rate bank account, in terms of an auxiliary signed measure nu and a canonical strategy theta built from the scale function and speed measure.
reason: Entirely a mathematical-finance proof paper: no tables, no figures, no data. Nothing empirical to reproduce.

method: Crosses four deep forecasting backbones (TimesNet, DLinear, N-BEATS, iTransformer) with three output heads (point/Huber, single-Gaussian NLL, K=4 Gaussian-mixture NLL) on S&P 500 monthly log-returns 1871-2023, under 5 anchored walk-forward folds x 3 seeds, scoring CRPS-skill, pinball, coverage, Diebold-Mariano and Model Confidence Set, plus ARIMA(2,0)/GARCH(1,1) classical baselines.
reason: The target series is a long monthly S&P 500 total/price return history, freely available from the Shiller (ie_data) CSV and, for the post-1927 portion, from Yahoo ^GSPC; the cross-asset panels are ordinary listed tickers. Everything else is model code with fully specified hyperparameters, so the head-vs-backbone gradient is directly rerunnable.
data_needed: S&P 500 monthly log-returns, 1871-01 to 2023-12 (1,832 months) - Shiller ie_data free CSV; post-1927 cross-check with Yahoo ^GSPC monthly
Cross-asset / cross-frequency generalisation panels (equity index and daily-frequency series) - Yahoo Finance daily and monthly closes
Risk-free rate for any excess-return variant - FRED DGS3MO / Ken French RF

Backbone spread within the Gaussian head at h=1 = 5.07 pp; within GMM head at h=1 = 3.9 pp

method: CLQT is a closed-loop LLM portfolio-manager benchmark: agents run a five-stage gather/synthesize/allocate/execute/reflect cycle over 26 bi-weekly rounds under a TimeGate, cost model and MCP tool layer, scored on a five-axis APM-CS capability scorecard, with an ablation grid and a live broker track on post-cutoff data.
reason: The headline validation is a live broker track on 18 NYSE days in June 2026 that is unseen post-cutoff by construction - rerunning it later cannot reproduce it. The backtest track additionally depends on a proprietary multi-provider news/sentiment channel registry and on stochastic LLM rollouts whose per-round allocations are not published as a fixed series, so the Sharpe and scorecard numbers are not recoverable from free data.

method: Trains a physics-informed DeepONet (hard-constrained ansatz plus residual-based adaptive refinement) to learn the Heston pricing operator across the whole parameter space, benchmarked against the semi-analytic Heston solution and a finite-difference solver.
reason: Training requires no labelled data at all - the loss is the Heston PDE residual on sampled collocation points - and every reported accuracy figure is measured against a synthetic semi-analytic benchmark. No market prices are used anywhere.

method: Formulates adaptive AI delegation as a Governance-Aware POMDP with Bayesian belief updating and a Belief-at-Risk penalty, then validates it with synthetic stress tests, confidence-only perturbations, forecast-accuracy sweeps, appetite sensitivity and a benchmark against five governance heuristics.
reason: Every reported number is generated from simulated AI-quality regimes (low-reliability, noisy, improving, high-reliability) with cached/perturbed AI confidence streams; the 'historical market replay' is only a backdrop for those synthetic AI evidence streams, which are not published. There is no empirical claim about market data that free prices could reproduce.

method: Derives the variance-optimal (Galtchouk-Kunita-Watanabe) hedge for claims on forward curves driven by an HJMM SPDE with infinite-rank stochastic covariance, proving density of finite-maturity strategies, convergence of finite-rank spectral projections, and an exact bucket/rank/residual decomposition of the quadratic hedging error.
reason: Illustrations are analytic examples in affine stochastic-covariance, multiplicative HJMM and CIR models. No dataset, no market forward curves, nothing empirical.

method: Trains deep-hedging RL agents under MSE, downside-risk and CVaR objectives to hedge swaptions with one to three swaps, benchmarked against sensitivity-based rho-hedging, with SHAP attribution and KAN-vs-FCNN comparison, plus misspecification stress on kappa and theta.
reason: All experiments run on paths simulated from a three-factor arbitrage-free dynamic Nelson-Siegel model; the hedging-error distributions and every performance metric are Monte-Carlo outputs, not measurements on real swaption or swap quotes. Swaption/swap-rate histories are also vendor-only.

method: Builds collective and individual actuarial risk models whose claim processes are driven by an underlying stochastic (SIS epidemic) population, derives scaling limits, and provides bounds and approximations for ruin probabilities.
reason: Purely theoretical with Monte-Carlo illustrations of the ruin-probability bounds under assumed parameters. No dataset, and the subject is insurance solvency rather than market data.

method: Introduces a regime-adaptive KS / GL-KS self-similarity test built on the discrete Grunwald-Letnikov fractional derivative, proves the filtered empirical-process limit and Hurst-estimator consistency, validates by Monte Carlo, then applies it to daily log-realized-volatility series and to daily equity-index log-price trajectories to classify rough volatility and (in)efficient market states.

The realized-volatility half needs an RV series (Oxford-Man style, intraday-derived) which is a weaker link, but the log-price Hurst table stands alone.
data_needed: Daily closes for the index panel - Yahoo tickers ^AEX, ^AORD, ^AXJO, ^BFX, ^BVSP, ^DJI, ^FCHI, ^FTSE, FTSEMIB.MI, ^GDAXI (plus the remaining realized-library indices), full history through ~2023, sample lengths 5,900-13,500 daily observations
Optional: daily realized-variance series for the same indices (Oxford-Man / realized-library archive) for the log-volatility table
Monte Carlo replication of fBm/fGn paths at H in {0.1,...,0.9}, N in {100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000} for the size/power tables
reproducible_targets: Indices where the unfiltered KS branch is selected instead: AXJO 0.4921 (0.4684-0.5159), BVSP 0.4875 (0.4631-0.5120), FCHI 0.4964 (0.4747-0.5181)

Empirical size of GL-KS in the long-memory regime stays near nominal (about 0.9-1.2% at 1%, 4.7-5.4% at 5%, 9.8-10.5% at 10%) while the unfiltered KS statistic inflates to 47.1% / 76.9% / 88.5% at N=100 and stays at 5.1% / 16.3% / 27.8% even at N=5,000

method: Builds a Bayesian pipeline with three arms: a discount-factor dynamic linear model for one-step-ahead log-realized-volatility and 95% VaR on S&P 500 daily returns (train 2000-2019, test 2020-01-02 to 2024-12-30), Bayesian logistic regression for card-fraud detection on IEEE-CIS, and a hierarchical Beta state-space model for compliance risk, comparing against GARCH(1,1)-t and an LSTM.
reason: The market arm is nothing but daily S&P 500 log-returns over 2000-2024, free from Yahoo ^GSPC, with fully specified models (DLM delta=0.98 beta=0.98, GARCH(1,1) with standardized-t, 2-layer 64-unit LSTM on |r| and r^2 with 30-step lookback) and standard Kupiec/Christoffersen backtests. The fraud arm uses the free IEEE-CIS Kaggle dataset. Only the realized-volatility target needs an intraday-derived RV proxy, which can be substituted.
data_needed: S&P 500 daily closes / log-returns 2000-01-01 to 2024-12-30 - Yahoo ^GSPC (train 2000-2019, out-of-sample T=1,257 days 2020-01-02 to 2024-12-30)
Daily realized-volatility proxy for the log-RV forecasting table (e.g. squared-return or range-based RV from ^GSPC OHLC, or an archived realized library)

method: Argues that temporal models fail on pure-price crypto prediction and instead proposes CryptoGAT, a lightweight correlation-graph attention network over the cross-section of coins, evaluated on daily OHLCV for 66 major cryptocurrencies (15/04/2023 to 08/01/2026, 999 trading days, 6:2:2 chronological split, 30-day lookback) against LSTM, GRU, ALSTM, PatchTST, iTransformer, StockMixer, TGN, Graphormer, MASTER, with IC/ICIR/Precision@N and a top-K long portfolio.

Market-cap screen (> $200M) to rebuild the universe - free CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap snapshot

method: Prices American options and flexible-forward FX contracts under a time-inhomogeneous Heston model via a recursive matrix-Riccati characteristic function and a Volterra early-exercise integral equation, solved with a double-COS expansion and a damped-Sinc local-basis scheme, benchmarked against a penalty-iteration MCS-ADI finite-difference solver.
reason: A numerical-methods paper: every table compares the new spectral schemes against an FD solver and against published Haentjens-in't Hout benchmark values on assumed parameter sets. No market FX or option quotes are used.

method: Multi-method event study of two Japanese bank M&A events - the October 3, 2005 MUFG creation and the April 1, 2018 Resona Holdings merger - estimating CARs with the market model, CAPM and Fama-French three-factor model over a +/-20-day window, then VAR/Granger causality and impulse responses for spillovers to other banks, plus propensity-score matching for the ATT.

Event dates and windows are published, so CARs and t-statistics are directly recomputable.

method: Studies a Stackelberg game where one reinsurer sets a common premium and invests, while many heterogeneous insurers choose retention and investment under relative-performance concerns; characterises follower equilibrium retention by a scalar fixed point, reduces the leader problem to one dimension, and proves finite-player to mean-field convergence.
reason: A game-theoretic paper whose figures are equilibrium maps and convergence plots computed from assumed parameter values. No dataset at all, and the domain is reinsurance pricing rather than traded markets.
